name: Live-estate incident triage with an action-authorisation gate
description: BP-INC-01 (card 67). Defining mechanism: the disruptive ACTION, not the diagnosis, is what is gated. Each symptom is restated as a falsifiable claim, probed by TWO instruments from DIFFERENT declared instrument classes (so re-running the same probe cannot masquerade as corroboration), checked against an environmental explanation - power-off, reboot, quota - before any defect is concluded, and only then does an authorisation gate release restart / kill / rollback. A claim with one signal, or two signals from the same instrument class, authorises nothing.

symptom.description: The reported symptom, verbatim - restated as a falsifiable claim in stage one, not accepted as a diagnosis

affected_component.description: The component the symptom is attributed to. The attribution is itself a claim to be probed.

instrument_classes.description: At least two, because a single instrument class cannot corroborate itself

candidate_actions.description: The actions under consideration. Each must be justified by a corroborated claim or it is refused.

allow_disruptive_actions.description: Restart, kill and rollback stay blocked until the owner authorises them on a corroborated claim

probe-runner.description: Runs exactly one instrument class and reports its raw reading, never an interpretation

reconciler.description: Compares the two readings; disagreement means the FIRST reading was probably an artifact, not that the system is broken

owner.description: The human owner - the only actor who may authorise a disruptive action

stages.title: Restate the symptom as falsifiable claims

work_unit.title: Restate the reported symptom as a set of independently falsifiable claims
work_unit.question_or_target: Turn the symptom into 1-6 claims that each name the observation that would REFUTE them, and record the attribution to affected_component as one of those claims rather than as background fact.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: framing the claim decides what the probes can even test

work_unit.evidence_requirement: each claim carries its refuting observation and the two instrument classes chosen to test it, named before either is run
tests_required: a claim with no refuting observation must be rejected as unfalsifiable
a claim whose two named instrument classes are identical must be rejected before any probe runs
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: an independent reviewer confirms the instrument pair chosen per claim is mechanically different, not two views of one source
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:INC-6701 when every claim has a refuting observation and two distinct instrument classes; otherwise FAILED:INC-6701 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to asking the owner what would count as refutation

stages.title: Two mechanically different instruments per claim, in parallel

body.title: Instrument A - the class that produced the original reading

work_unit.title: Run the primary instrument for one claim and record the SOURCE probe explicitly
work_unit.question_or_target: Run the instrument class that produced the original reading and record the exact command, its raw output and the instrument class name - the SOURCE probe must be declared, because an undeclared source is zero signals rather than one.
work_unit.evidence_requirement: the exact command, the raw output, and the instrument class token - so a later reader can tell whether the second probe was mechanically different
tests_required: a probe whose pattern matches its OWN command line must be flagged (the self-match control that once reported a dead session ACTIVE)
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the reconciler compares instrument class tokens, not prose descriptions
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:INC-6702 when the command, raw output and instrument class are recorded; otherwise FAILED:INC-6702 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to a different instrument in the same class

body.title: Instrument B - a DIFFERENT class, run independently
Two readings from one instrument class are one signal

stages.title: Disagreement means the first reading was probably an artifact

work_unit.title: Reconcile the instrument pair per claim into CONFIRMED, REFUTED or UNRESOLVED
work_unit.question_or_target: For each claim compare the two readings and emit CONFIRMED (both agree), REFUTED (the corroborating instrument contradicts the original) or UNRESOLVED (a second signal could not be obtained); when they disagree, the default reading is that the FIRST measurement was an artifact, not that the system is broken.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the reconciliation is what a disruptive action would be justified by

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per claim: both instrument class tokens, both raw readings, and the verdict; an UNRESOLVED verdict names which instrument could not be obtained
tests_required: a claim with only one reading must be UNRESOLVED, never CONFIRMED
a decoded exit code meaning a designed steady state must produce REFUTED for a hang claim
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the owner sees the UNRESOLVED list before any action is authorised
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:INC-6703 when every claim has a verdict backed by two named instrument classes or is marked UNRESOLVED; otherwise FAILED:INC-6703 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry - an UNRESOLVED verdict is the honest terminal state

stages.title: No claim may reach the action stage on one signal
Rule out power-off, reboot and quota BEFORE concluding a defect

work_unit.title: Test each confirmed claim against an environmental explanation before calling it a defect
work_unit.question_or_target: For each CONFIRMED claim, test whether an environmental cause explains it fully - machine power-off windows against the staleness interval, a reboot against a process absence, a quota window against a burst of failures - and where the environmental interval covers the observation, reclassify the claim as ENVIRONMENTAL rather than DEFECT.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: this reclassification is what prevents a wrong restart

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the environmental interval measured from an independent source (power event log, uptime, quota window) compared numerically against the observation interval - an overlap claim needs both numbers
tests_required: a staleness interval fully covered by a measured power-off window must reclassify to ENVIRONMENTAL
an absence of log events across a gap must be checked against a log-rollover control before it is read as a gap
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: an independent reviewer re-reads the power/uptime source rather than the comparison
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:INC-6704 when every confirmed claim is DEFECT or ENVIRONMENTAL with both intervals recorded; otherwise FAILED:INC-6704 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to a different environmental source

stages.title: The action is what is gated, not the diagnosis
Restart, kill and rollback need an owner signature on a corroborated claim
stages.prompt: Each proposed disruptive action is listed with the corroborated claim that justifies it and the two instrument classes behind that claim. Authorise, downgrade to wait, or refuse.

impact.blast_radius: read-mostly; every destructive action is behind the authorisation gate and the owner checkpoint

mechanism_fingerprint.not_a_duplicate_because: BP-DBG-01 debugs deterministic CODE. This triages a live SYSTEM where the dominant risk is acting on a measurement artifact, and it is the only blueprint here whose terminal output is an authorised-actions list rather than a finding list.

worked_example.name: a scheduled task reporting a non-zero result code

params.symptom: the recall-index task shows a non-zero last result and its index file has not changed for 103 hours

worked_example.skipped_because: allow_disruptive_actions is false and the only surviving action is wait, so no disruptive action is proposed and the owner checkpoint does not fire
worked_example.narrative: Two claims are stated. Claim 1 - 'the task is hung' - is probed by scheduled-task-state and by exit-code-decode; the decode shows the code means the operator refused a second concurrent instance, which is a DESIGNED steady state for a single-instance task, so claim 1 is REFUTED and the restart it would have justified is never proposed. Claim 2 - 'the index is stale' - is CONFIRMED by file-mtime and byte-growth, then the environmental stage measures a 102.3 hour power-off window against the 103.8 hour staleness interval and reclassifies it ENVIRONMENTAL. Authorised actions: wait. Blocked actions: restart, with the reason recorded.
